headline: Less clicking.
More doing.
slides.description: Ask in the side panel. Foxl reads, clicks and types in your real Chrome tabs.
slides.alt: Foxl's actual side panel next to an example research page, with a request to collect three useful points and a plain-text answer.

headline: Get to the point.
Stay on the page.
slides.description: Turn a long page into a clear summary, right beside what you are reading.
slides.detail: Read a page. Ask a follow-up. Keep your place.
slides.alt: The actual Foxl side panel summarizing a local example article, with the article still visible beside it.

headline: Three tabs.
One clear answer.
slides.description: Ask Foxl to read across tabs and bring the useful details together.
slides.detail: Open, switch and group tabs as the task needs.
slides.alt: Foxl's actual tab context chips and a plain-text comparison of three fictional venues displayed beside a demo comparison page.

headline: Let Foxl do the steps.
Stay in control.
slides.description: Fill fields and move through pages. See when Foxl is working, and stop it from the page.
slides.detail: The activity border and Stop Foxl control are built in.
slides.alt: Foxl working on a local demonstration form with the shipping teal activity border and Stop Foxl control, beside the actual side panel.

headline: Your desktop agent.
Now in Chrome.
slides.description: Install Foxl Desktop and keep it running. The extension connects on the same computer.
slides.alt: The exact Foxl Desktop is required first-run state next to a three-step installation explanation.
